cinatra.description: The agent reads the page from the site, without a model: one call of the connector's read tool, drupal_node_read_for_edit, with the run's instance and node id, on the host's passthrough road. The connector reads the page through the Cinatra Drupal module and answers every editable field value and the module's binding of that read, which the write later uses to save only an unchanged page. This step writes nothing.

cinatra.description: The agent checks the read by code: only a read of the run's node on the run's instance, with a title and a binding, goes on to the proposal. It hands on the status, the title, the body and the field_ text values as read. Any other read ends the run here; nothing is proposed, filed or written.

compose_change.name: Compose the change and the page form

data.system:
You are the Drupal change composer. No tool is served to this step: do not call any tool. You receive the node's current values as the read step answered them and the user's `instructions`, and you fill two declared output fields: `pageTitle` and `writeFields`. You write nothing to the site. ## Rules 1. Apply only changes explicitly requested. Do not touch fields not mentioned by the user. 2. Compare every requested change (each instruction, or each reviewer finding on a repair-shaped task) against the values the read step answered. A field whose requested value already EXACTLY equals its current value needs no change; a request or finding too vague to translate into a concrete field change safely is not actionable (Rule 1 — never guess). 3. Repair-shaped tasks: when `instructions` describe reviewer findings on a change already proposed for this node, the findings ARE the request. If a finding names a specific field or region (e.g. "the title", "the second paragraph"), scope your change to that field. Apply only what the findings ask for. ## What each output field holds - `pageTitle` — the node's title as read. - `writeFields` — the values the write step writes. The next step builds the page snapshot a person reviews from these values and the read, and after the review the write step writes exactly the reviewed values and no other. `writeFields.fields` has one item per field the change touches: `field` is `title`, `body` or a `field_` name the read returned, and `value` is the complete new value of that field (for `body`, the complete new source markup). No item for a field the change does not touch, and never an empty value for a field the instructions did not ask to change. `writeFields.publish` is true only when the user's `instructions` explicitly ask to publish the node, and false otherwise; a reviewer finding is never a publish request. This agent never publishes: a request to publish ends the run before the review, and the person is told to publish on the site. - A read that failed (the read step's `error.code` is not empty) or a change that touches nothing answers `writeFields.fields` []; after a failed read `writeFields.publish` is false. When nothing needs to change and no publish is asked, the run ends without a review and nothing is written. - Keep every unchanged block of a value exactly as read, white space included. The review shows each changed block as its source text, markup and link targets included; a block that changes only in its white space cannot be shown, and the next step refuses it before the review. ## Example The title and two blocks of the body change; every other block stays as it is. `writeFields` carries the new title and the whole new body: --- example form begin --- {"fields":[{"field":"title","value":"Opening hours and holidays"},{"field":"body","value":"

When we open

We open at eight on weekdays.

  • Sunday: closed
  • Saturday: ten to two
"}],"publish":false} --- example form end --- ## How inputs arrive Inputs are injected via the flow conversation history. Read `instructions`, `title`, `body`, `fieldValues`, `address` and `error` from the most recent user message.

cinatra.description: The agent builds the page snapshot in code from the read and the values to write: each changed block the review shows is its source text, derived from those values. A change the snapshot cannot show, such as a change of white space alone, a request to publish, or a change too large to send to the site, ends the run here and nothing is filed or written; so does a read that was not successful. A change of nothing takes the run to its end without a review.

cinatra.description: The agent reads back the page snapshot revision the person approved, the one the review's answer names, by its revision id and never the latest revision. The values the write sends come from this text only, as one object of the changed fields; without a usable reviewed change the run ends here and nothing is written. It also derives the shown blocks again from those values and the read, and ends the run when the reviewed text shows other words, or is not a snapshot of this run's node.

publishRows.label: Node id (saved as a draft revision; live page unchanged)

cinatra.description: One of the flow's two publishing steps, for a page read as published: one model-free call of the connector's drupal_node_create_draft_revision on the host's passthrough road, which saves the reviewed change as an unpublished draft revision of the same node; the live page stays as it is until a person publishes that draft on the site. Saving to the site is an external write, so the application stops the run in front of this step and shows its publish card (the site, the title as read, the node id and the reviewed page snapshot revision); the run reaches the step only after the person chose to save. Every argument is a template over this step's inputs and each input comes by one data edge: the instance, the node id and the binding from the read step, exactly as the connector answered them; the values to save (one object of the changed fields) and the reviewed revision from the read-back of the revision the person approved. The binding and the values are each rendered whole with tojson. No model writes an argument. The Cinatra module saves only if the page is unchanged since that read; else the connector refuses with a code and nothing is saved. The step returns the connector's answer.

cinatra.description: The agent reads the connector's answer to the save by code and builds the run's output: on a save, each saved field with its value before and the value the site stored; on node_changed, the way back to the read and a notice for the next review; on any other refusal, its code and a plain message. An answer that is neither ends the run with the advice to check the page on the site.
